nodes.summary: The branches of the loop closed by `p` in `P`: the pairs of `P` strictly inside `p` that are not strictly inside another pair of `P` strictly inside `p`.
nodes.title: Branches of a loop closed by a base pair

nodes.summary: `q` lies strictly inside the pair `p`: `p.1 < q.1` and `q.2 < p.2`.
nodes.title: Strict enclosure of one base pair by another

nodes.summary: In a secondary structure every pair is either an exterior branch or a branch of exactly one pair of the structure (and not both): each pair is shared by the loop it closes and exactly one enclosing loop, possibly the exterior loop.
nodes.title: Unique loop decomposition

nodes.summary: Every position has a unique innermost strict container (not loop membership): a position `x` either lies strictly inside no pair, or there is a unique pair `p` with `p.1 < x < p.2` such that no branch of `p` has `x` strictly inside it. This is an innermost-container assignment, not the conventional loop decomposition of positions: endpoints are excluded from the loop they close (a position `x = q.1` or `x = q.2` is…
nodes.title: Every position has a unique innermost strict container

nodes.summary: The exterior branches of `P`: the pairs not strictly inside any pair of `P`.
nodes.title: Exterior branches of a secondary structure

nodes.summary: The free energy of a structure in the loop model: the sum of the energies of the loops closed by its pairs (the exterior loop contributes `0`).
nodes.title: Free energy of a structure in the loop model

nodes.summary: The energy of the loop closed by `p = (i, j)` in `P`: a hairpin with no branch, a stack, bulge or interior loop with one branch `(k, l)`, and the affine multiloop energy `a + b · r + c · u` with `r ≥ 2` branches and `u = (j - i - 1) - ∑ (l - k + 1)` unpaired bases.
nodes.title: Energy of the loop closed by a base pair

nodes.summary: A pair with no branch closes a hairpin loop.
nodes.title: A pair with no branch closes a hairpin loop

nodes.summary: A pair with exactly one branch `q` closes a stack, bulge or interior loop with inner pair `q`.
nodes.title: A pair with one branch closes a stack, bulge or interior loop

nodes.summary: A pair with at least two branches closes a multiloop with the affine energy.
nodes.title: A pair with two or more branches closes a multiloop

nodes.summary: A loop (nearest-neighbor) energy model: energies of hairpin loops closed by `(i, j)`, of stacks, bulges and interior loops closed by `(i, j)` with inner pair `(k, l)`, and the affine multiloop parameters `a` (per multiloop), `b` (per branch) and `c` (per unpaired base). The exterior loop has energy `0`. Units: free energy, e.g. kcal/mol.
nodes.title: Nearest-neighbor loop energy model

nodes.summary: The exterior-loop recursion on the prefix `[0, len)`: `W(0) = 0` and `W(len + 1) = min (W(len), min_{i ≤ len} W(i) + V(i, len + 1 - i))` (the last base is unpaired, or closes an exterior branch `(i, len)`).
nodes.title: Zuker exterior-loop recursion

nodes.summary: Zuker's algorithm (Zuker and Stiegler 1981; Zuker and Sankoff 1984), here with the affine multiloop energy of Jaeger, Turner and Zuker (1989): the Zuker recursion computes the minimum free energy over all secondary structures on `s` with minimum hairpin `m`, for any real loop energies (of either sign). The minimum ranges over a finite set that contains the empty structure, so it is never `⊤`.
nodes.title: Zuker's algorithm

nodes.summary: The minimum free energy is at most `0`, the energy of the open chain (the empty structure).
nodes.title: Minimum free energy is at most zero

nodes.summary: Zuker's minimum free energy of `s`: the exterior recursion on the whole sequence.
nodes.title: Zuker minimum free energy

nodes.summary: Zuker's recursion on the interval `[i, i + len)`, with `j = i + len - 1`, returning `(V, WM)`: the least of the hairpin energy `hairpin i j`, the interior-loop energies `interior i j k l + V(k, l)` over `i < k < l < j`, and the multiloop energies `a + WM(i + 1, u) + WM(u + 1, j - 1)` over `i < u < j - 1`; unpaired base) is the least of `V + b`, `WM(i + 1, j) + c` (base `i` unpaired), `WM(i, j - 1) + c` (base `j`…
nodes.title: Zuker's recursion

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
